vectors.title: A newer snapshot omitting an earlier revocation is refused; the revoked set only grows
Sync never activates, withdraws or changes unrelated rows; it only records and appends revokes
Withdraw at equal or lower epoch is refused; strictly higher naming the current row is accepted
Activating a revoked pair (same or pre-revoked epoch) is refused; the revoked pair is never resurrected
The only way past a revoked row is a fresh higher-epoch select naming that row; the revoked pair stays revoked
A revoked issuer key revokes rows it signed (cause kept distinct) and blocks new statements under that key
Replaying an older select, an already-applied select or a withdrawn statement changes nothing
cites: R3 no implicit reactivation through replay

vectors.title: Reactivation after withdrawal needs a fresh higher-epoch select naming the withdrawn row
Withdraw with no row, wrong predecessor, unverified, or over a revoked row is refused
Every rejected transition leaves exactly one preserved negative-evidence record; accepts leave none
A withdraw at an epoch already in the revoked set is refused
A withdraw signed under a revoked issuer key is refused with the distinct cause; the row stays active
Record-level revocation: a higher epoch naming the revoked row cannot carry the revoked record back in; a different valid record is accepted
A record revoked before any activation is refused at every epoch; the scope is explicit (record id and version), another version is a different record
Issuer-level revocation covers every key of the issuer: a higher epoch under a fresh key of a revoked issuer is refused; another issuer is accepted; a withdraw under the revoked issuer is refused
Key-level revocation: a higher epoch signed by the revoked key is refused at every epoch; another key of the issuer is accepted; the key stays revoked
Selection-level revocation is specific to the old identity: a fresh higher-epoch selection of the same valid record is accepted, the revoked identity stays revoked permanently
A snapshot revoking the record revokes the row; the guard never passes it and a higher epoch of the record is refused
